opening.headline: We explore how to understand data processing requirements by country—separating them into processing location, storage location, and data residency—and how to select appropriate provider options for each.
body: When a product is used in multiple countries, customer requirements differ. Some customers require inference to run solely within their own jurisdiction, while others demand a documented guarantee that data is not stored. These requirements may appear similar but address distinct issues. Data non-storage and processing within a specific region are separate configurations.

In this course, we first compare the non-retain options offered by Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic. We then examine regional processing and data residency options, as well as how cross-region inference conflicts with residency requirements. Finally, we explain cases where model availability decreases when regions are fixed, and how to transform national requirements into option design.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can explain the meaning of the no-preservation and region-specific processing options.
Can be categorized into requirements by country, preserving, processing, and storing, and appropriately responding to the relevant options.

screens.title: Data processing requirements vary by country.
screens.lead: First, read the requirements that products serving multiple countries face. The diagram shows national requirements divided into three different types of questions.

visual.alt: A diagram dividing national requirements into three questions: preservation, processing location, and storage location.
labels: U.S. customer: inference limited to domestic use
European customers: Submit documentation regarding data storage location
Medical customer: Does not retain prompts or responses
Processing location: Where is inference executed?
Storage location: Where is the stored data located?
Retention: for how long, and what is being retained?

paragraphs: This is a hypothetical scenario. A product is provided to enterprise customers in multiple countries. U.S. customers require inference to be executed solely within the United States. European customers request documentation confirming where their data is stored. Customers in the healthcare sector require the condition that prompts and responses are not retained.

These three requirements are all related to data, but they ask different questions. The first concerns processing location, the second concerns storage location, and the third concerns retention. Suppliers' documentation also sets these three aspects separately. For example, Anthropic sets inference location and storage location as two independent settings.

There's one more conflict here. If a region is fixed, you can only use the models and features provided within that region. This results in fewer available models as you attempt to meet residency requirements.

callout.label: Questions to be answered in this class
callout.text: How to respond to national requirements with respect to no-preservation and location-specific processing options?

screens.outro: First, let us recall the requirements our service has encountered.

screens.title: Think of countries with data residency requirements
screens.lead: First, think through each question on your own before selecting an answer. The instructor's thoughts will then be organized and presented. No answers are submitted.

items.prompt: Among the countries we serve, are there any that have data residency requirements?
items.answer: If required, it is likely mentioned in the contract or security checklist. It is important not to simply list the country name, but to verify the original text in which the requirement is stated.

items.prompt: Is this requirement about how long prompts and responses are stored?
items.answer: This is a requirement regarding retention. It is addressed by configuring settings that either disable logging or limit the retention period. This is independent of the processing location.

items.prompt: Is the requirement about where inference is executed?
items.answer: This is a requirement regarding processing location. It corresponds to request-specific regional parameters, region-specific endpoints, or region selection.

items.prompt: Are you inquiring about where the stored data is located?
items.answer: This is regarding requirements for storage locations. Storage locations are often set separately from processing locations, and it is easy to mistakenly fix one while overlooking the other.

screens.outro: We have distinguished three cases; therefore, let us first compare the three providers with regard to retention options.

screens.title: Non-preservation: 3rd party preservation and log options
screens.lead: Select each tab to review the default retention policies and methods for achieving no retention specific to each provider.

tabs.label: Google
tabs.body:
**Basic Principle.** The document states the principle that customer data is not used for model training without explicit consent.

**Data Retention.** In the Models as a Service offering, limited-duration data is retained in certain areas. For example, prompt logging for abuse detection.

**How to Achieve Data Non-retention.** To achieve data non-retention, customers must take specific actions in each area. Since a single setting does not cover all areas, retention must be verified on a per-area basis.

tabs.label: OpenAI
tabs.body:
**Basic.** Data sent via API is, by default, not used for model training.

**Retention.** Abuse monitoring logs are generated for all API feature usage and are retained by default for up to 30 days. Retention periods longer than 30 days may be extended if legally required.

**How to achieve zero retention.** Both Zero Data Retention and Modified Abuse Monitoring exclude customer content from abuse monitoring logs. Both controls require prior approval from OpenAI and acceptance of additional requirements, and are selected at the organization or project level.

tabs.label: Anthropic
tabs.body:
**Basic.** Dialogue content, i.e., prompts and outputs, is generally not retained. The exception is Covered Models, which require retention for 30 days.

**Retention by Function.** There are cases where data retention is mandatory based on specific functions; the retention policies and durations by function are specified in the respective function documentation.

**How to Achieve Non-Retention.** The Claude API provides two data processing modes: ZDR and HIPAA-compliant processing. ZDR must be requested through the sales team at the organizational level and must be activated separately for each organization. The applicability of each feature is indicated in the eligibility matrix.

tabs.label: General Caution
tabs.body: Non-retention must be verified sentence by sentence against the requirements in the documentation. Excluding data from logs is not the same as ensuring data is never stored anywhere. When using models on Amazon Bedrock or Google platforms, the cloud provider acts as the data processor, and therefore the documentation of that provider must be followed.

screens.outro: We have organized the preservation now, so let's look at how to set the processing location and storage location.

data.notes: The table shows that processing location and storage location are independently configurable. Even if inference is fixed in the United States, the storage location must be separately specified. After fixing a region, you must verify whether a request was actually processed within that region through responses or usage reports. The Usage API enables regional routing checks by aggregating usage data via `inference_geo`.

screens.outro: Narrowing the processing scope is advantageous for residence requirements but comes at the cost of losing other aspects. Let us examine the trade-off through cross-region inference.

screens.title: Cross-region inference: What is gained versus what is lost when expanding the scope
screens.lead: Move the slider to adjust the cross-region inference range of Snowflake Cortex from the widest to the narrowest setting. Observe how the model selection breadth and residency requirements change as the range adjusts.

visual.alt: Diagram showing horizontally four stages representing the narrowing of the cross-region inference range from a broad stage to a narrow stage.
labels: Broadness: advantageous in model selection range, throughput, resilience, and cost

stops.body: This offers the widest scope. The request can be processed in any region or cloud supported by Snowflake. It provides the broadest model selection, high throughput, strong resilience, and the lowest cost. It is not suitable for customers with strict residency requirements.

Processes only within the specified cloud provider, such as AWS_GLOBAL, AZURE_GLOBAL, or GCP_GLOBAL. Used when data must remain within a specific cloud provider's network, maintaining a certain level of low cost and high throughput.

Processes only within specific regions of designated cloud providers, such as AWS_US, AWS_EU, AZURE_EU. While this limits operations to the provider and geographic scope to meet regional requirements, models outside of that region cannot be used.

Processed only within the home region of the account. While meeting the strictest residency requirements, you can only use models and features deployed within that region. The document states that it is suitable for use cases that do not require the latest model.

screens.outro: The document states that, even during cross-region inference, customer data is stored in the account region, and inputs and outputs are temporarily transferred only during processing and are not stored in the processing region. Let us now examine this contradiction as a concrete example.

screens.title: Commentary: Conflict of fixing the region reduces the available models
screens.lead: The instructor breaks down the scenario step by step. Select the right arrow to proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Verify the example
steps.body: We have fixed the processing region to Europe as per European customer requirements. However, the new model that the team would like to use is not yet available in that region. We now face a conflict between residency requirements and model selection.

steps.title: Distinguish what is required
steps.body: Review the customer's requirements document again to determine whether the request pertains to processing, storage, or retention. If processing is fixed when only storage is required, it may have unnecessarily narrowed the scope.

steps.title: Checks the list of supported locations
steps.body: Check whether the supplier's support location list provides the required models and features for that region. Feature support varies by location. Make sure to verify both the availability of the model and the presence of any required additional features. Google indicates that feature support differs by region.

steps.title: The options are summarized into three.
steps.body: If not provided, there are three options: use the previous model supported in that region, establish cross-region paths within the scope permitted by requirements, or re-negotiate with the customer and requirements.

steps.title: Compare the impact of options
steps.body: This compares three options based on three criteria: model quality, cost, and extent of meeting residence requirements. The previous model may have subpar quality, may fail to meet regional requirements, and requires significant time for re-negotiation. Internal stakeholders and customers must jointly determine which criterion is most important.

steps.title: Leaves results and evidence behind
steps.body: Records the selected results and rationale in documentation. It should be possible to reassess when customer requirements or supplier support scope change. When the same scenario repeats, this record significantly reduces judgment time.

screens.outro: Next, we will examine the process of converting country-specific requirements into option design, looking at the code and configuration.

screens.title: Explanation: The order of converting country-specific requirements into option design
screens.lead: The following is an example of national requirements migrated into supplier options. The countries and requirements are hypothetical, and the option names are as listed in the document. Please read the right-side explanation in sequence.

data.code:
#Example with requirements moved as options (country and requirement are hypothetical)
#US customer: Inference should be executed only within the US -> request-specific inference_geo
import anthropic

client = anthropic.Anthropic()

response = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-opus-5-5",
    max_tokens=1024,
    inference_geo="us",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Summarize the key clauses of this contract."}],
)

#Actually, it confirms from the response where the inference was executed.
print(response.usage.inference_geo)

#European customers: Must be processed only within the home region of the account -> Disable cross-region inference (Snowflake example)
# ALTER ACCOUNT SET CORTEX_ENABLED_CROSS_REGION = 'DISABLED';

#Customers whose processing can remain within the cloud boundary -> Cloud scope
# ALTER ACCOUNT SET CORTEX_ENABLED_CROSS_REGION = 'AWS_GLOBAL';

notes.note: U.S. customer requirements specify the processing location. If `inference_geo="us"` is provided for each request, inference will run exclusively on U.S. infrastructure. This parameter can only be used with supported models; using it with unsupported models results in a 400 error.

Verify that the request was executed at the intended location using the `usage` value in the response. Without validation, relying solely on configuration, you would not be able to detect if the request executed at a location different from intent. Across the organization, usage reports are aggregated using `inference_geo` for review.

European customers require that account operations be performed only within the home region. In Snowflake, setting the cross-region scope to `DISABLED` achieves this. Instead, only models deployed in the home region can be used.

For customers whose requirements can be met entirely within the cloud boundary, we allow broader ranges such as `AWS_GLOBAL` to achieve greater model selection flexibility and throughput. Confirm whether the requirement refers to a geographic region or the cloud boundary itself, and then proceed accordingly.

screens.outro: I will finalize by confirming the flow: present requirements in tabular form, map them to options, restrict scope to workspaces, and validate the response accordingly.

screens.title: Summary: Regional requirements constrain model selection
screens.lead: Summarize the content discussed so far. Please read the following paragraphs in sequence.

paragraphs: Non-preservation refers to a setting regarding preservation, regional processing refers to a setting regarding the location of processing, and data residency refers to a requirement regarding the storage location. These are distinct settings, and satisfying one does not imply that the other two are also satisfied.

The narrower the processing scope, the more advantageous it is for residency requirements, but it becomes less favorable in terms of available models and features, throughput, and cost. Conversely, expanding the scope improves choice and cost, but may conflict with residency requirements. This trade-off cannot be eliminated, and a decision must be made on where to draw the line based on specific requirements. The first step is to read whether the requirement document specifies both processing location and storage location.

The design process follows a fixed sequence. National requirements are categorized into preserve, process, and store, and are presented in a table. Each requirement is matched against supplier options, workspaces or projects are divided by nation to limit allowed and base regions, and the actual processing location is validated through response and usage reports. Results and justifications are documented, and the requirements are re-evaluated if they change.

glossary.def: This setting does not store prompts or responses or exclude them from logs. Separate requests or approvals are required per provider.
An option that restricts inference execution to a specific request or workspace unit.
Requirements regarding the geographic location where data is stored and processed.
This approach sends the request to available capacity outside the account's home region. Expanding the scope increases the choice of options but may conflict with residency requirements.

misconceptions.myth: If no preservation is required, regional requirements are satisfied.
misconceptions.fact: Retention status and processing location, storage location are separate settings. Inference can be executed in a different region even if data is not retained.

misconceptions.myth: You can use all models even if the region is fixed to one.
misconceptions.fact: Functionality and model support vary by region. When a region is fixed, only the models available in that region can be used, thereby reducing the selection options.

misconceptions.myth: Cross-region inference stores data in another location.
misconceptions.fact: Snowflake documents that customer data is stored within the account region and is temporarily transferred to the processing region only during input and output operations, without being stored in the processing region. However, since the processing location may change, this could conflict with processing location requirements.

closing.lead: Summarizes the key points of this class.
points: Non-preservation, region-specific processing, data residency preservation, processing location, storage location are different settings.
Cross-region inference is advantageous in terms of selection breadth and cost, but may conflict with residency requirements.
List the requirements in a table and map them to options, then verify the actual processing location.
closing.reflectionLead: The following questions are for self-thinking purposes only and will not be submitted or graded.
closing.reflection: What aspect of our country-specific requirements applies to retention, processing location, or storage location?

checks.q: The requirement document from the customer states that "prompt and response storage is not required." To satisfy this requirement, what setting should be first verified?
options: Setting to fix the inference region to the regional endpoint of the customer's country
Whether zero data retention (such as zero data retention) is applied and prior approval for data retention controls
Configuration that maximizes the cross-region inference scope
Data residency setting with storage location placed in the account region
checks.explain: Retention, processing location, and storage location are separately configured. Preservation restrictions are related to retention requirements and thus should be addressed through preservation controls such as "no retention"; for some cases, prior approval or actions by the customer may be necessary.

wrong.0: Regional fixation determines the processing location but does not change whether log retention is enabled.
wrong.2: The cross-region scope relates to settings concerning selection range and throughput and is unrelated to preservation.
wrong.3: Specifying a storage location does not eliminate the act of preservation itself.
